subject.title: fix(plugins): surface oversized-file warnings in doctor migration reads

question: Should doctor treat legacy plugin state above 10 MiB as unsupported and leave it unmigrated with a warning, or must it provide a supported recovery path that preserves existing user state?
rationale: The descriptor technique is mechanically sound, but choosing to reject previously readable persisted state is an upgrade-policy decision with user-state consequences.

options.title: Preserve upgrade recovery
options.body: Define and test a supported recovery path for oversized legacy state while retaining descriptor-bound allocation limits.

options.title: Accept the cap as unsupported legacy state
options.body: Explicitly approve the 10 MiB cutoff, document the user recovery process, and prove the doctor warning directs users to it.

recommendation.title: Preserve upgrade recovery
recommendation.body: Define and test a supported recovery path for oversized legacy state while retaining descriptor-bound allocation limits.

likelyOwner.reason: Low-confidence adjacent routing candidate for a cross-plugin migration-contract decision.
